title: A daily word
tomorrow: why does one blessing come after the plate is empty?

segments.voice: Yesterday, three times a day: three stops, and the line morning, noon, night. Today, what to carry into one of those stops.

Ten tabs open. Three podcasts half-finished. An article saved for later and never opened. Taking in a lot can add up to keeping very little. Acts praises one town for something smaller. When Paul came to Berea, the people there opened the scriptures to check what he told them. They “searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” Daily. Not everything at once.
screen: `TEN TABS OPEN.` → `BEREA CHECKED THE TEXT.` → `DAILY, NOT ALL AT ONCE.`

segments.voice: Psalm one sets the same pace for the one it calls blessed: “his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.” Delight first, then meditate. A word to chew on, not a chore to finish. Luke shows how it's done. After the shepherds come to the manger and go, “Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.” Kept, like something precious in a pocket. Pondered, turned over and over. That's a daily word. One passage, read slowly: maybe a chapter, maybe one verse that stops you. Then it gets carried, and taken out again at lunch. When Jesus is tempted in the wilderness, he answers with scripture: “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” Bread is daily. So is the word. Here's where it meets an ordinary week. A hard conversation is coming, or a decision, or a worry that won't sit still. A line read slowly in the morning can be there when it's needed, the way a verse was there for Jesus in the wilderness. Some Christians follow a reading plan, some open a devotional, some read straight through a Gospel. The pace matters more than the plan: a little, every day, slowly.
screen: `DELIGHT FIRST, THEN MEDITATE.` · `MARY KEPT AND PONDERED.` · `BREAD IS DAILY. SO IS THE WORD.` · `THERE WHEN IT'S NEEDED.` · then, large: `A WORD A DAY.`

segments.voice: If a Bible or a Bible app is nearby, open to Psalm one and read it slowly, once, under your breath. Then stay with the single line that caught you. If nothing's at hand, stay with Mary's two verbs instead: kept, and pondered.
A daily word. One passage of scripture, read slowly each day and carried, the way Mary kept hers.
Hold onto this: a word a day, kept and pondered, not finished and filed. That's day 1685.

howItsDone: Some Christians read a set passage each day from a reading plan, a lectionary or a devotional book, reading slowly and returning to a line through the day.

chat.says: Pop's eyes are tired, so i read him his chapter. he stops EVERY verse to talk. an hour??
options: That's the pace. Mary kept and pondered. He's chewing it, not racing it.
Gently speed him up. The goal is to get through the whole Bible.
Read it to him faster, then talk at the end so you finish.
chat.meaning: A daily word is one passage read slowly and turned over, like Mary pondering. His stopping to talk is the pondering.
